 James Harden accumulated 13 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Bucks.
 With the Cavaliers getting dominant efforts from Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen, they didn’t need much from Harden or Donovan Mitchell (15/4/3 with two three-pointers) on Saturday. However, fantasy managers rostering either guard likely hoped for more production. Harden played 26 minutes on Saturday, checking out for the last time with 2:45 remaining in the third quarter. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 James Harden led the Cavaliers with 24 points (7-of-14 FGs), five rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers in a 114-111 loss to the Hawks on Thursday. 
 Harden has been underwhelming this season, with his scoring, assists and shooting efficiency all down. However, he was able to get his shot going in this one, and he ended up scoring at least 20 points for the first time this season while also having his best field goal percentage of the season. However, the trade-off was a new season low for assists. Harden should be better as the season progresses, but he may not play to his third-round ADP.

 James Harden produced 22 points (8-of-18 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, nine assists, two steals and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Timberwolves. 
 After scoring two points on 1-of-6 shooting in the first half, Harden stepped up in the second half. He scored 20 points after halftime, 15 of them in the third and fourth quarters. Harden scored five of Cleveland’s 14 points in overtime, helping the Cavaliers hand Minnesota its first loss of the season.

 James Harden tallied 16 points (5-of-12 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Thursday’s loss to the 76ers. 
 Harden was limited to six points in the first half of Thursday’s season opener, then scored 10 after halftime. However, ball control was an issue in the second half, as the Cavaliers’ point guard turned the ball over four times. As a team, Cleveland committed 15 turnovers in the second half, which helped them blow a 29-point lead. Harden and the Cavs will look to bounce back on Saturday when they host the Nets.

 James Harden recorded 24 points (7-of-10 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s exhibition against the Magic. 
 Harden made his first appearance of the preseason on Sunday, and the veteran point guard looked sharp. Shooting 70 percent from the field, “The Beard” logged 26 minutes in the first three quarters before calling it a night. While Harden’s current ADP puts him on the back end of the third round in 12-team leagues, he can offer greater value than that.

 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that James Harden has signed a three-year, $97 million extension to remain with the Cavaliers. 
 Harden’s new deal includes a trade kicker and a player option, so he’ll retain some form of control over his future. The superstar guard was traded from the Clippers midseason, and Cleveland made the Eastern Conference Finals. The team will look to continue its upward trajectory with the pairing of Harden and Donovan Mitchell, and the former is still a reliable fantasy option heading into his 18th season.

 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that James Harden is declining his player option for next season and negotiating a new multiyear deal with the Cavaliers. 
 Harden, who helped the Cavaliers reach the Eastern Conference Finals last season, would have earned a base salary of $42.3 million had he opted into the final season of his contract. However, the decision to opt out and negotiate a new deal with the Cavaliers is likely to benefit both parties. While Harden would get additional security in the form of more years, Cleveland may be able to give him a lower annual salary. With the team hopeful to retain pending free agent Dean Wade while also lowering its payroll, every little bit helps.

 James Harden finished Monday’s Game 4 loss to the Knicks with 12 points (2-of-8 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, one steal and one blocked shot. 
 Harden struggled throughout the Eastern Conference Finals, and Monday’s 130-93 defeat was no different. In addition to shooting 25 percent from the field, the veteran guard was a brutal 0-of-6 from beyond the arc. And for the 33rd time in his postseason career, Harden finished a game with more turnovers (five) than made field goals. He has a player option for 2026-27 worth just over $42.3 million, but there’s always the possibility that Harden and the Cavaliers agree to an extension with a lower annual salary. From the trade deadline onward, he provided second-round value in eight-cat formats. Expecting similar production from Harden next season would be realistic, even with the poor showing in the conference finals.

 James Harden accounted for 19 points (8-of-15 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Saturday’s Game 3 loss to the Knicks. 
 While more productive in Game 3 than he was in either of the first two games of the Eastern Conference Finals, Harden’s overall impact was once again muted. Given the matchup, the Cavaliers can ill afford not to have Harden playing at an elite level. He shot just 1-of-7 from beyond the arc on Saturday and finished with as many turnovers as assists. Harden and the Cavaliers need a win on Monday to avoid getting swept.

 James Harden tallied 18 points (6-of-15 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), six rebounds, two assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Thursday’s Game 2 loss to the Knicks. 
 After racking up six turnovers and getting torched defensively by Jalen Brunson in Game 1, Harden recorded a better stat line on Thursday. While the field-goal percentage remained low, The Beard did not commit a turnover in 32 minutes. However, he had just two assists, a byproduct of the Cavaliers’ shooting 38.8 percent from the field and 9-of-35 from three. The Cavaliers will hope that Harden can find his groove in Game 3 on Saturday, as they sit in a 0-2 hole.

 James Harden produced 15 points (5-of-16 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in the loss to the Knicks on Tuesday. 
 Harden had a rough Tuesday night at MSG. He struggled with his shot, particularly from beyond the arc, failed to generate points for his teammates, and turned the ball over six times. Additionally, he was the defensive target the Knicks repeatedly aimed for during the fourth quarter and overtime, as New York walked down Cleveland and overcame a 22-point comeback. Harden will almost certainly need to be better going forward for the Cavaliers to win games in this series. He’ll have a chance to bounce back in Game 2 on Thursday.

 Joan Beringer finished Saturday’s loss to the Spurs with 12 points (4-of-8 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), six rebounds, two assists and one steal.
 Beringer made his first start of the season on Saturday, as Rudy Gobert (back) was out. Unfortunately for the second-year center, he had to match up with countryman Victor Wembanyama. Beringer played 34 minutes, and his points and rebounds production were solid. If Gobert remains out for Monday’s matchup with the Bucks, that will likely be a more manageable assignment for Beringer.
